function: Implicit CSI feedback: compression and reconstruction of eigenvector precoders with an autoencoder trained on digital-twin channels and fine-tuned on real-world measurements (pp. 2-3).
system: Single-user MIMO-OFDM, 8-patch antennas at BS and UE, 2 spatial streams, 3.8 GHz, 100 MHz, 1,620 subcarriers, indoor corridor; no RIS (p. 3).
method: EVCsiNet autoencoder (UE encoder, BS decoder, 2-bit quantizer) with MSE reconstruction loss on digital-twin data, then online fine-tuning of the decoder only with real-world data (pp. 2-4).
data_channel: Wireless InSite ray-traced digital twins (indoor, outdoor) for training, 3GPP TR 38.901 CDL for the baseline; own 3.8 GHz measurements at 78 points for fine-tuning and testing (pp. 3-4).
test_conditions: Train on DT or CDL data; test on real-world corridor data, directly or after fine-tuning with 30% of points; also changed BS antenna with 5% fine-tuning (pp. 3-5).
baselines: Type II codebook with 2, 3, 4 beams (3GPP, non-learned); EVCsiNet variants trained on outdoor DT or 3GPP CDL data; no other learned CSI-feedback model (pp. 4-5).
metrics: Cosine similarity rho of reconstructed precoders; feedback bits; real-world throughput (Mbps) with an EP MIMO detector (Table II, Fig. 4; pp. 3-5).
q1_support: p. 3: "RW measurements were conducted in an indoor corridor"; the model is fine-tuned and tested on the authors' own 3.8 GHz measurements. p. 4: "trained on the standardized Cluster Delay Line (CDL) model from 3GPP TR 38.901" is used only for a baseline.
q2_support: p. 4: "directly applying the Indoor EVCsiNet to RW scenarios yields suboptimal performance"; the DT-trained model is tested on real-world data. p. 3: "30% of the RW measurement points in Fig. 2(b) were randomly selected" for fine-tuning; p. 5: "Incorporating 5% of new BS antenna data into OL restores" performance.
q3_support: p. 4: "We evaluate three EVCsiNet variants"; the learned models compared are the same network trained on indoor DT, outdoor DT or CDL data, and the Type II codebook is the only other method, so no earlier learned method of the same class is compared apart from these variants.
q4_support: p. 2: "designed for reduced computational complexity and latency"; p. 3: "this OL approach introduces minimal communication and computation overhead"; both are qualitative and the 32 feedback bits are signaling overhead, so no order, FLOPs, parameters or runtime is reported.
q5_support: p. 3: "Data were collected at 78 marked points, with 200 measurements per point"; the model is fine-tuned and tested on measured data, which the criterion accepts, but no link, DOI or release statement for the code or the dataset appears in the paper.
notes: q1 is met through the real-world measurements (p. 3), not through the Wireless InSite digital twin, which is a site-specific ray-tracing model built by the authors (pp. 2-3); the 3GPP CDL model appears only in a baseline (p. 4). q5 is met only through the clause on measured data: the dataset is the authors' own and no release is stated, so the reviewer should confirm that reading. q3 is 0 because every learned comparison is EVCsiNet of [5] (p. 2) trained on other data; the reviewer may instead count the CDL-trained EVCsiNet, which the paper calls the baseline (p. 4), as the earlier learned method of [5]. The test split of the real-world data after fine-tuning on 30% of the points is not detailed (p. 3). The PDF is arXiv 2505.00660v2 of 2 May 2025 and prints no DOI; its title and first authors match the Crossref record of the DOI.
